facts.text: I have a large patch of dead skin on my left thigh.

facts.item: lump on the thigh before the dead skin
facts.text: It started as a lump, about 4 by 5 cm, in the same spot.
I noticed the lump in April.
Over two weeks it turned into dead skin.
It's on the right side of my chest.
I haven't been taking any medicines.
Nobody in my family has a blood-clotting disorder.

findings.name: skin examination
findings.result: 20 × 18 cm area of cutaneous necrosis on the left thigh.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: Leukocytosis (white blood cells 36.59 × 10^9/L) with hypereosinophilia (eosinophils 21.15 × 10^9/L; 57.8%); thrombocytopenia (platelets 19 × 10^9/L).

findings.name: liver function tests
findings.result: Elevated: ALT 178 IU/L; AST 68 IU/L; GGT 329 IU/L.

findings.name: coagulation studies
findings.result: Fibrinogen 4.15 g/L (elevated); D-dimer 82.20 mg/L FEU (markedly increased).

findings.name: allergic, parasitic, rheumatologic and immunologic workup
chest CT
findings.result: Bilateral patchy pulmonary opacities and a small pleural effusion.

findings.name: skin biopsy of the thigh lesion
findings.result: Dermal necrosis and hemorrhage with perivascular lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils.

gold.reasoning: 1. Other allergic, parasitic, rheumatologic, and immunologic disorders were excluded — “The workup for allergic, parasitic, rheumatologic, and immunologic diseases was unremarkable.” 2. Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis was considered among skin-eosinophil syndromes — “Differential diagnosis may include eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis…” 3. Purpura fulminans was considered among causes of cutaneous necrosis — “…purpura fulminans…” 4. Eosinophilic cellulitis was considered among eosinophilic skin conditions — “…and eosinophilic cellulitis.”

notes: Index visit: the admission in May 2013 for the thigh necrosis, at which he also reported right-sided chest pain and bloody sputum (s001-s008).
The April nodule and its evolution are history of the presenting complaint (f002-f007); its absent redness, itch and pain are children of the nodule.
Fever is denied twice (s003, s004) and is one fact citing both.
